column3: Manual trigger completes without the 5-minute wait
column4: Publish a docs_article entry in Sandbox, then manually run the "Promote CS Docs from Sandbox to Prod (Staging env)" workflow (Actions tab, Run workflow, leave entry_uids blank). Confirms the manual path is a genuine on-demand shortcut, not just an early cron tick.
column6: Merged a real test article into main (PR #400) under cs-docs/agent-os/automations/automation-management/, which synced into Sandbox as a draft. Published it in Sandbox, then manually triggered the workflow (scoped via entry_uids rather than leaving it blank, to avoid sweeping in unrelated real content). The run completed in 52 seconds. This workflow only has a workflow_dispatch trigger and no schedule at all, so any completion here is proof of a genuine on-demand path, not an early cron tick.

column3: Save a draft without publishing
column4: Save/update an entry without publishing it, then manually run the promotion workflow. Since the script only ever fetches published entries, the draft should not be promoted at all.
column6: Used the same GitHub-synced entry while it was still an unpublished draft (before publishing it for scenario 1). Ran the promotion workflow scoped to its uid. Run log showed "No published entries to promote": the draft never appeared in the promotable list at all, and no entry was created in Prod.

column3: Unpublish an entry
column4: Unpublish an entry that previously existed in Prod, then manually run promotion. Confirms an unpublished entry is never (re-)promoted, and any existing Prod copy is left untouched rather than deleted (the script only creates/updates, never deletes).
column6: Using the same entry already promoted to Prod in scenario 1, unpublished it in Sandbox and re-ran the promotion workflow scoped to its uid. Run log showed "No published entries to promote". Verified via the management API that the Prod entry's _version and publish_details (staging + development timestamps) were byte-for-byte unchanged, and its reference inside the "Automation Management" nav node was still present. This confirms the existing Prod copy was left untouched, not deleted or modified.

column3: Verify promoted content matches Sandbox exactly
column4: Publish an entry, run promotion, then check the resulting Prod entry's content (fields, body/sections, tags, SEO description) matches Sandbox exactly.
column6: Published two throwaway articles, each with an embedded local image, under cs-docs/assets/asset-localization/ via PR #405, merged to main, synced to Sandbox, published, and promoted. Diffed Sandbox against Prod field by field for both entries: title, url, tags, body HTML, and the embedded image reference were identical. The only difference found was an internal block _metadata.uid, which the code's own comments already document as expected to regenerate per stack, not a real content mismatch. Finding: the promoted image was never re-uploaded to Prod's own asset library. The Prod entry's img tag still points at the Sandbox stack's asset host (api key blt1a9af0bcb3816d6e), so Prod's rendered content stays dependent on that Sandbox asset continuing to exist. Both staging and development publish_details were present and correct for both entries. Alpha: Sandbox uid blte54bef176f74da3f, Prod uid blt95a08745b669dff7, staging URL https://stag-www.contentstack.com/docs/assets/test-promotion-image-alpha-1786984556. Beta: Sandbox uid blt34f4dc0563d86280, Prod uid blt4101aa315b0e372c, staging URL https://stag-www.contentstack.com/docs/assets/test-promotion-image-beta-1786984556.

column3: Two different entries published together get promoted together
column4: Publish two different entries, then run promotion once. Confirms a single run (with entry_uids left blank) picks up and promotes every currently published entry, not just one.
column6: Published both of the same two test articles from scenario 4 in Sandbox, then ran the promotion workflow once, scoped to both entry uids. The run log showed "Found 2 published entries to promote", and both were created in Prod and linked into the live "Asset Localization" nav section within that same run. Finding: both entries carried the same pr-405 tag from the same merged PR, so both tried to create a Release named "PR #405". The first succeeded. The second failed with HTTP 422 ("name is not unique"), caught and logged as a warning rather than failing the run. Only the first entry and the shared product_navigation entry ended up in the Release. The second entry was correctly created and nav-linked in Prod but was silently left out of the Release. Beta ran first and is in the Release: Sandbox uid blt34f4dc0563d86280, Prod uid blt4101aa315b0e372c, staging URL https://stag-www.contentstack.com/docs/assets/test-promotion-image-beta-1786984556. Alpha ran second and was left out of the Release: Sandbox uid blte54bef176f74da3f, Prod uid blt95a08745b669dff7, staging URL https://stag-www.contentstack.com/docs/assets/test-promotion-image-alpha-1786984556.

column3: Re-running promotion with no changes is a clean no-op
column4: Run promotion, then immediately run it again with nothing changed in between. Confirms the second run skips every entry as unchanged rather than re-writing or erroring.
column6: Created two throwaway articles (Alpha, Beta) under cs-docs/assets/asset-localization/ via PR #427, merged to main, published in Sandbox, and promoted in one run. Beta: Sandbox uid blt9b173a9e9283d18f, Prod uid bltbf79af7f625b1d2f, staging URL https://stag-www.contentstack.com/docs/assets/test-sbprod-round2-beta-1787032278. Alpha: Sandbox uid blt30f10446558fe9e7, Prod uid blt12dfcf541a2cf9b6, staging URL https://stag-www.contentstack.com/docs/assets/test-sbprod-round2-alpha-1787032278. Re-ran promotion immediately with nothing changed. The run reported "Updated" for both entries, not skipped, even though nothing had changed. Root cause: on creation, Contentstack's Management API regenerates the modular block's internal _metadata.uid inside article_content, and this nested field is never stripped by contentsEqual, which only strips top-level fields on the entry itself, not metadata nested inside a block. So the first re-run after any entry's creation always looks changed and forces a real update, which then overwrites Prod's block uid to match Sandbox's. A third run, with still nothing changed, correctly reported both entries as skipped, and _version/updated_at stayed unchanged, confirming a true no-op from that point on.

column3: entry_uids input scopes to a single entry
column4: Manually run promotion with a single entry's ID in the entry_uids field. Check the run log confirms only that entry was processed, and other currently-published entries were left untouched by this run.

column3: entry_uids input scopes to multiple entries
column4: Manually run promotion with several comma-separated entry IDs in entry_uids. Confirms all and only those entries are processed in that run.

column3: entry_uids with a nonexistent or unpublished ID
column4: Manually run promotion with an entry_uids value that doesn't match any currently published entry (typo, already-unpublished, or fake ID). Confirms the run completes cleanly and promotes nothing, rather than erroring.

column3: Cron doesn't double-promote after a manual run
column4: After a manual promotion, wait for the next scheduled cron tick (every 5 minutes) and confirm its promote step logs a no-op for the entries the manual run already handled.
column6: After the baseline manual run for the same Alpha and Beta entries (see scenario 6), waited for a real scheduled cron tick, which fired at 06:16:37 UTC. That run was unscoped (entry_uids blank) and swept in 4 published entries stack wide. Its log showed both Alpha and Beta reported as "No changes detected, skipping", confirming cron did not redo the manual run's already-finished work. The 2 entries it did update were unrelated real content elsewhere in the stack.

column3: Manual trigger racing a cron tick
column4: Manually trigger the workflow at (or very close to) the moment a scheduled cron tick is also due. Confirms the shared concurrency lock serializes the two runs instead of letting them act on Prod at the same time.
column6: Edited Alpha's content and timed a manual dispatch to fire right at a due 5-minute cron mark. Finding: GitHub's scheduled trigger for this workflow fired roughly 51 minutes late relative to its nominal 5-minute cadence, a known GitHub Actions platform behavior where schedule events can be delayed under load. This makes precisely timing a manual run against a real cron tick impractical. Proved the serialization directly instead: fired two manual workflow_dispatch runs 5 seconds apart, scoped to the same two entries. The shared concurrency group (sandbox-to-prod-promote-csdocs) queued the second run rather than letting it run concurrently. Run 1 executed 07:08:57 to 07:09:32 UTC. Run 2 did not start its job until 07:09:35, after run 1 released the lock, and correctly found nothing left to do since run 1 had already applied the edit.

column3: Publish a Release with several entries at once
column4: Publish a Release containing 5-10 entries at once, then run promotion once. Confirms every entry in the Release is promoted in that single run, since one run scans all currently-published entries rather than reacting per-entry.

column3: Publish then unpublish before the next run
column4: Publish a new entry, then unpublish it again before the next promotion run (cron or manual) executes. Confirms it never reaches Prod at all.

column3: Edit an existing Prod entry then unpublish before the next run
column4: Publish an edit to an entry that already exists in Prod, then unpublish it again before the next promotion run. Confirms Prod keeps its last-published-and-still-current content, not the since-unpublished edit.
column6: Reused Beta (see scenario 6 for uids). Made a first edit to its content, published it, and promoted it, which became the new current baseline in Prod (version 3). Made a second, different edit, then published and unpublished it again before the next run. The run log showed "No published entries to promote", and Prod's Beta entry content matched exactly the first edit, confirming Prod kept the last published and still current content rather than the later unpublished edit.

column3: Rapidly toggle publish/unpublish then run promotion
column4: Toggle an entry publish/unpublish/publish a few times in quick succession, then run promotion once. Confirms whichever state the entry is actually in at run time is what ends up in Prod.
column6: Reused Alpha (see scenario 6 for uids). Toggled its publish state five times in quick succession (publish, unpublish, publish, unpublish, publish), ending on a known, distinct published content state, then immediately ran promotion once scoped to it. Prod's Alpha entry was updated to exactly that final published content, confirming the pipeline picks up whatever state the entry is actually in at run time rather than any intermediate toggle.

column3: Run logs clearly state per-entry outcomes
column4: After a promotion run, check the GitHub Actions log clearly states each entry's outcome (created / updated / skipped-no-op) so a human can tell what happened without guessing.

column3: Manual workflow only promotes
column4: cron workflow does both steps
column5: Confirm the manual "Promote CS Docs from Sandbox to Prod" workflow only runs the Sandbox-to-Prod promote step, while the scheduled cron workflow always runs promote followed by the Prod-to-GitHub pull step, in that order.

column3: Entry of a different content type is never touched
column4: If a non-docs_article entry exists in the Sandbox stack, run promotion and confirm it's never fetched or processed (the sync is scoped to docs_article at the client level, independent of any trigger).

column3: Product resolves from Sandbox breadcrumb for all 13 products
column4: For each of the 13 products in product-registry.ts, an entry carrying that product's sandboxBreadcrumbUid resolves to the correct cs-docs folder slug. Covers the core fix: the old code only knew assets and headless-cms.

column3: Product resolves from Prod breadcrumb for all 13 products
column4: Same as above but using prodBreadcrumbUid, since afterCreate runs against the Prod entry whose breadcrumb was already remapped.

column3: lytics-cdp resolves by folder, not by its /lytics/ url
column4: An article with url /lytics/... and the Lytics CDP breadcrumb resolves to lytics-cdp. This is the regression a url-based fix would introduce, since folder and url namespace deliberately differ.

column3: developer-resources resolves despite carrying another product's url
column4: Articles with /headless-cms/, /administration/ and /developers/ urls all resolve to developer-resources when their breadcrumb says so.

column3: Multi-variant products resolve from either variant
column4: agent-os (Automate Connectors / Automate Guides) and marketplace (Marketplace Apps / Marketplace Platform Guides) each have two breadcrumb uids
column5: and both map to the single folder slug.

column3: Falls back to product tag then title marker
column4: With no usable breadcrumb, resolution uses the product-<slug> tag, then the [Marker] title prefix, in that order.

column3: Never guesses the product from the url
column4: An entry with no breadcrumb, no product tag and no title marker returns linked:false with a reason, rather than deriving a product from its url.

column3: Flat product links into an existing section
column4: An Assets article tagged nav-subsection-overview appends a docs_article reference into the existing Overview nav_section, touching only the product_navigation entry.

column3: Nested product creates the full chain
column4: A Headless CMS article tagged nav-subsection-introduction/core-concepts/basics creates both missing links_2026 levels, reports both as created nodes, and republishes every one.

column3: Existing chain is descended, not recreated
column4: When a links_2026 node with a matching title already exists, it is reused. It is still reported as touched, because its nested_links were rewritten and its published version would otherwise go stale.

column3: Top-level doc lands in the existing blank-header section
column4: An Analytics article tagged nav-toplevel (file sits directly in cs-docs/analytics/) appends into the existing blank-header nav_section and does not disturb named sections.

column3: Top-level doc creates a blank-header section when none exists
column4: For a product with no blank-header section, a nav-toplevel article causes one to be created and flagged as a structural change.

column3: Re-linking the same entry is idempotent
column4: Running the link twice adds exactly one reference, not two.

column3: Unlinkable entry never fails the promotion
column4: Unresolvable product, missing placement tag, and missing product_navigation entry each return linked:false with a stated reason instead of throwing.

column3: Publish targets staging and development only
column4: PROMOTION_ENVIRONMENTS is exactly [staging, development] and contains nothing matching /prod/i, so automation can never publish to Production.

column4: npm run nav-link-audit cross-checks all 13 product-registry.ts navUids against .nav-tree.json.

column4: npm run nav-link-audit replays placement for every cs-docs markdown file. FAQ/troubleshooting files (doc_type: faq) are excluded since they become product_faqs_2026, not docs_article.

column3: Environment preflight fails loudly on a missing environment
column4: verifyPromotionEnvironments lists /v3/environments once per run and throws naming the missing environment, rather than failing one publish at a time.

column3: Release contains the full nav chain
column4: After promoting a new entry, the PR-named Release holds the docs_article, its product_navigation entry, and every links_2026 node in the chain.

column3: Every touched entry is published to both environments
column4: After promotion, each touched entry shows publish details for staging and development.

column3: Second entry from the same PR reuses the existing Release instead of racing on create
column4: Unit test: call createReleaseForPromotion twice in the same run with the same PR number but different entries (the exact Alpha/Beta shape from Round 1 scenario 5), against a fake Contentstack client. Confirms createRelease is only called once and both entries' items are added to that same release uid.
column6: tools/cs-sync/src/test-release-manager.ts, test 'second entry from the same PR in the same run reuses the existing release instead of racing on create'. Fix: createReleaseForPromotion now calls the new findReleaseByName(`PR #<n>`) before createRelease. If found, it reuses that release instead of attempting a second create that would 422 on the duplicate name.

column3: Entries from different PRs still get their own separate Releases
column4: Unit test: call createReleaseForPromotion for PR #405 then again for PR #406, each with a different entry. Confirms the fix's reuse logic is scoped by PR number and doesn't accidentally merge unrelated PRs into one Release.
column6: tools/cs-sync/src/test-release-manager.ts, test 'entries from different PRs get different releases'. createReleaseCalls was 2, and the two returned release uids were different.

column3: First entry for a PR still creates the Release when none exists yet
column4: Unit test: call createReleaseForPromotion once for a PR number with no prior Release. Confirms the find-then-create fix didn't regress the original single-entry-per-PR path from Round 1 scenario 4.
column6: tools/cs-sync/src/test-release-manager.ts, test 'first entry for a PR creates the release'. findReleaseByName returned null, createRelease was called exactly once, and the item was added to it.

column3: Live stack: two entries from the same PR, promoted together, both land in one Release
column4: Re-run the exact scenario from Round 1 #5 (two docs from the same merged PR, published together, promoted in one run) against a live Sandbox/Prod stack now that the fix is deployed. Confirms both entries end up in the same 'PR #<n>' Release this time, closing out the original bug report, and that findReleaseByName's pagination/response parsing works against the real /v3/releases endpoint (only inferred from code, not yet confirmed live).
